stories.headline: Toto Wolff explains why George Russell skipped media duty after Kimi Antonelli F1 title win
stories.summary: George Russell skipped media duties after the Mexico City Grand Prix as boss Toto Wolff admitted his driver was suffering a "catastrophic moment" with teammate Kimi Antonelli celebrating winning the world championship.
stories.body:
George Russell skipped media duties after the Mexico City Grand Prix as boss Toto Wolff admitted his driver was suffering a "catastrophic moment" with teammate Kimi Antonelli celebrating winning the world championship.

Russell, 28, was the heavy pre-season title favourite but Antonelli has turned the tables on his experienced team-mate to become the youngest champion in F1 history.

The 20-year-old has nine wins to Russell's three, storming to the championship in just his second season in the sport.

Russell admitted this week that this has been the most disappointing season of his career, at the moment he needed to deliver most.

He graciously congratulated Antonelli in the moments after the race, before Mercedes allowed him to leave the track.

"He's distraught about the situation. It was a great show of sportsmanship to go and see Kimi," Wolff said.

"I have known George for such a long time and I know for a sportsperson, for a racing driver, this is a catastrophic moment.

"I've been in situations where it's very, very difficult to cope. So him not doing the media work or leaving the track is absolutely understandable. Him staying would have actually surprised me."

- The families that built Kimi Antonelli, F1 world champion

- In pictures: The moments that defined Kimi Antonelli's F1 title-winning season

Mercedes were fined 5,000 euros by the FIA due to Russell's non-appearance post-race.

Russell started Sunday's race from second but was swallowed up by a host of cars on the run down to turn one as his Mercedes appeared to struggle for power.

He then bashed into Red Bull's Isack Hadjar, being hit with a 10-second penalty, and ended the race sixth.

Russell is now fourth in the drivers' championship having been leapfrogged by Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton.

"Maybe the race was a little bit a picture of his season. This was a race for him to win. We had the pace in the car," Wolff added.

"And we let him down on the first straight. The energy delivery is not what we thought it should be. And so I'm very much with him at the moment."

stories.headline: Karl Bushby: Hull City welcome adventurer home after 28-year trek from Chile
stories.summary: British adventurer Karl Bushby is set to complete his 28-year trek from South America to Hull on Monday and he has been supported by the Premier League club.
stories.body:
British adventurer Karl Bushby is set to complete his 31,000-mile, 28-year trek from South America to Hull on Monday and he has been supported by the Premier League club who called on fans to welcome him to City Hall.

At the age of 29, Bushby left Punta Aires, Chile, in 1998 with the aim of walking back home without breaking two self-imposed rules: not to return to the UK until he had completed his journey and not to use transport to advance his mission.

The former paratrooper, now aged 57, will be met by his mother, son and granddaughter when he arrives in his hometown of Hull to end his 28-year odyssey.

"Odysseus was a bit of an amateur. But, you know, I'll cut him some slack -- I haven't met any giant Cyclops," Bushby told The Independent.

While crossing four continents, Bushby has overcome deserts, mountains, jungles and the frozen Bering Strait between Alaska and Russia.

Along the way he says he has had a stand-off with a Polar Bear, entered crocodile-infested water to avoid a guerilla war in Colombia and been rescued from an ice floe by a helicopter.

Bushby swam the English Channel on Oct. 5 to begin the last leg of journey. He has spent the time since walking north, pushing his two-wheeled supply cart which he refers to as "The Beast."

Before crossing the Humber, Bushby recorded a video for Hull City fans which was posted by the Premier League club on Saturday following their 2-2 draw with Ipswich Town at the MKM Stadium.

"Quick shoutout to the lads and lasses in the stadium. Just to let you guys know I'm sitting on the other side of the Humber right here," he said while wearing a Hull shirt.

"Tomorrow I'm crossing that bridge and I'll be back in the city. I'm looking at being back int he city on Monday morning at around 11 'o clock. Would be great to se you all there.

"At some point I'm going to be joining you in the stadium to see a match."

He is due to make his final stop at Queen Victoria Square in the city centre before returning to his mother's house. His mother, Angela, has said she will be waiting to greet him at the garden gate.

stories.headline: Jayden Daniels throws TD pass and Commanders shut out Eagles over final 3 quarters in 27-10 win
stories.summary: — The Washington Commanders had just under two weeks to sit with their disheartening start to the season before their matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday night.
stories.body:
LANDOVER, Md. -- — The Washington Commanders had just under two weeks to sit with their disheartening start to the season before their matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday night.


Coming off a bye week, they still needed an extra 10 or so minutes.


Washington pulled together after an extraordinarily sloppy first quarter to score 27 straight points in a 27-10 victory. It was Washington’s first win in more than a month, and Philadelphia’s sixth straight loss.


“When you come off of a bye, you either rev right up or you need a minute to warm up — and we took a minute,” Washington coach Dan Quinn said.


The Commanders (2-4-1) committed a bevy of first-quarter penalties, which put them behind 10-0.


Jayden Daniels threw for 217 yards and a touchdown, as the offense got rolling. Aided by a defense that pitched a shutout for the final three-plus quarters, Daniels had time to build rapport with his receivers absent Terry McLaurin. The victory was Daniels’ first as a starter since beating the Los Angeles Chargers on Oct. 5, 2025.


“It’s a blessing from God just to go out there, and everything I’ve been through in my career so far,” Daniels said. “From different injuries and a lot of different setbacks."


The Commanders sacked Tanner McKee five times and intercepted one of his passes while holding the Eagles to 268 yards — just 199 before the meaningless final drive.


In his third start of the season in place of the injured Jalen Hurts, McKee threw for 212 yards without a touchdown. And prior to the final drive of the game, the Eagles' longest drive was 52 yards.


“We just made adjustments,” cornerback Trey Amos said. “We started a little bit slow, those things will happen sometimes, but after those adjustments, everybody came together to try and figure out a plan. It worked out, later down the line, series, quarters.”


Saquon Barkley ran for a touchdown for the Eagles but was held to 30 yards on 13 carries. Philadelphia finished with 91 yards rushing.


“I know nobody feels sorry for us, that’s for damn sure,” coach Nick Sirianni said. “Everyone is going to give us their best shot. I know nobody feels sorry for us and we have to do everything we can do to fix it so we don’t have this feeling for the last six games. Obviously, it sucks."


Both teams committed costly penalties. The Eagles’ Jake Elliott made a field goal to cut Washington’s lead to three points in the fourth quarter, but he had to try again because of an illegal formation penalty and missed from 41 yards.


Drew Stevens kicked four field goals for Washington, including a 56-yarder late in the first quarter. Daniels connected with Stefon Diggs for an 8-yard touchdown strike in the second quarter that tied it at 10l, and Washington led 13-10 at halftime.


The Commanders had a sloppy first few drives. Stevens missed his first field goal attempt, from 55 yards, and Chig Okonkwo lost a fumble.


Barkley’s 3-yard touchdown run put Philadelphia ahead 10-0 in the first quarter.


On Washington’s final drive of the first half, Daniels took a hard hit and was slow to get to his feet, but he stayed in the game as the Commanders finished with 27 straight points.


The Commanders remain in the hunt in a weak NFC East, two games behind the first-place New York Giants, despite opening the season with just one win in their first six games.


The Eagles, on the other hand, are in last place.


“Are teams taking shots at us? Yeah,” Barkley said. “We’re not the big bad Eagles anymore.”


Injuries
Eagles: Safety Michael Carter suffered an abdominal injury.


Commanders: Running back Jeremy McNichols limped to the locker room in the second half with a left foot injury.


Up next
Eagles: Host the Giants on Sunday.


Commanders: Host the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday.

stories.headline: Red Sox, Diamondbacks lead Gold Glove winners with 3 apiece
stories.summary: First basemen Christian Walker of Houston and Matt Olson of Atlanta won their fourth Gold Gloves on Sunday while Boston right fielder Wilyer Abreu won the fielding honor for the third year in a row.
stories.body:
ST. LOUIS -- First basemen Christian Walker of Houston and Matt Olson of Atlanta won their fourth Gold Gloves on Sunday while Boston right fielder Wilyer Abreu won the fielding honor for the third year in a row.

The Red Sox and Arizona tied for the high with three Gold Glove winners each. Red Sox center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela earned the honor for the second straight season and third baseman Caleb Durbin was a first-time winner.

Diamondbacks catcher Gabriel Moreno won his second Gold Glove, his first since 2023, while shortstop Geraldo Perdomo and right fielder Corbin Carroll were first-time winners.

Walker added to Gold Gloves he won in 2022-24. Olson also earned the honor in 2018, 2019 and 2025.

Braves utility man Mauricio Dubón won his third Gold Glove after 2023 and 2025.

Other second-time winners included Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman and center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong, New York Yankees left fielder Cody Bellinger, Detroit catcher Dillon Dingler and Milwaukee second baseman Brice Turang.

Additional first-time winners included Cleveland pitcher Tanner Bibee, Milwaukee left fielder Jackson Chourio, Texas utility man Ezequiel Duran, New York Mets pitcher Nolan McLean, Tampa Bay shortstop Taylor Walls and Seattle second baseman Cole Young.

Voting was conducted among managers and up to six coaches from each team, who can't select players on their own club. Since 2013, voting has been factored with a Society for American Baseball Research defensive index, which comprises about 25% of the total.

The utility category is based on a SABR formula and additional defensive statistics.

Walker earned a $75,000 bonus for winning the honor, Bibee $50,000 and Turang $25,000.

stories.headline: Messi brings Miami back to stun Revs, clinch Champions Cup spot
stories.summary: Inter Miami CF beat the New England Revolution 2-1 on Sunday in Foxborough, Massachusetts, with Lionel Messi once again providing the magic touch, this time to ensure his team's spot in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup.
stories.body:
Inter Miami CF beat the New England Revolution 2-1 on Sunday in Foxborough, Massachusetts, with Lionel Messi once again providing the magic touch, this time to ensure his team's spot in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup.

The win also helped Miami leapfrog the Revs into second place in the Eastern Conference with one game remaining in the MLS regular season.

"It makes me very happy for the players and for the club, we are on the side of contributing things," Miami manager Cristian González said after the game. "We are at a club that is in continuous growth, I have players committed to us. We needed to win and we challenged ourselves on what kind of team we wanted to be."

The Revolution edged out Inter Miami in the first half, registering six total shots, five corner kicks and generating an expected goals of .75, but the match went to the break tied 0-0.

Dániel Gazdag then opened up the scoring in the initial minutes of the second half, connecting with Ilay Feingold inside the box before finding the back of the net.

Miami found a way to respond to Gazdag's strike with a goal from Germán Berterame -- set up by a deft backward header from Messi -- in the 69th minute. González then bolstered Inter Miami's attack after drawing level, substituting in Luis Suárez, who had started Miami's last 25 games.

"We knew we were going up against a rival that tries to seek out duels where they defend high, so the possibility of changes was to have depth, look for the spaces, and the one-on-one matchups. We struggled with ball possession, which at times was very passive," said González. "My message to the players is I need everyone. In this case, we believed we needed to make some changes.

"This doesn't mean this is the team that's going to start the playoffs. Everyone shows me they're eager to want to play."

Messi doubled the score for Inter Miami, dribbling past defenders outside the box and smashing a trademark low, left-footed shot past Revs keeper Matt Turner.

The Revolution almost found their way back for a draw, but Ian Fray's own goal was quickly ruled offside to let Miami off the hook after it looked like Messi's heroics had been undone.

Ultimately, it was Messi's goal that clinched Inter Miami a spot in the 2027 Champions Cup. Had Miami lost or tied the game against the Revs they would have had work left to do on Decision Day on Nov. 7 to get into North America's top club competition.

"I have no doubt that he's the best of all," González said of Messi. None of them can compare to him when it comes to respect for his colleagues. Leo at his age and what he does, from my point of view, deserves the MVP and also the Ballon d'Or. I hope he can achieve it."

Inter Miami now joins Nashville SC, the Revs and the Vancouver Whitecaps in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup. The winner of the 2026 MLS Cup will also have a place in the Champions Cup.

The Herons now have 59 points from 33 games, and will finish the regular season with a home game against Charlotte FC that will have seeding implications ahead of the MLS playoffs.

stories.headline: How the Golden State Valkyries won the 2026 WNBA title in just two years
stories.summary: When Golden State joined the WNBA, the owner said the team would win a title within five years. The Valkyries did it in two.
stories.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- Almost exactly two years ago, Natalie Nakase sat across from Golden State owner Joe Lacob for her job interview to become the head coach of the WNBA's newest team, the Valkyries. It was October 2024, and Nakase had walked into the interview with notes on why she would be the best fit, her vision for how to build a team and what set her apart from her colleagues.

But the first 10 minutes of the conversation were led by Lacob: He told Nakase he likes to set incredibly high goals and shared how he plans to achieve them. Nakase sat up straighter and leaned in a few inches closer, enticed by Lacob's work ethic.

Near the end of the conversation, Lacob told Nakase the ultimate goal, the same one he had shared in the news conference announcing the creation of the team a year earlier: "We're going to win a championship in five years."

She slammed her fists on the table in front of them.

"Hell yeah, we're gonna win a championship," she said.

On Saturday, the Golden State Valkyries did just that, beating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals to win their first title.

Lacob and Nakase were wrong about one thing, though. The Valkyries didn't win their first championship in five years. They did it in two.

"I walked out of that conversation with Joe like, 'I want to work for him,'" Nakase said. "More than that, I want to win that first championship for him."

After the interview, Nakase immediately called her mentors, asking them how she could deliver on Lacob's aspirations. Their biggest piece of advice was to build a clear culture, and do it with competitors who would sacrifice anything for the group.

Along with general manager Ohemaa Nyanin, Nakase set the identity she wanted for her team: scrappy, defensive-minded, no egos. The Valkyries built the team their way, facing external scrutiny nearly every step of the way. People gawked -- or even laughed -- at Lacob's proclamation. But Nakase stood strong in her belief, and in his.

Sitting next to the championship trophy with a beer in her hand Saturday, Nakase was asked if winning the title felt as she imagined it would.

"F--- yeah."

TOGETHER, NYANIN AND Nakase handpicked the players who make up Golden State's roster. During the 2024 expansion draft, the Valkyries acquired Veronica Burton, the gritty two-way guard, and Kayla Thornton, a reigning WNBA champion -- two cornerstones of the franchise -- as well as Cecilia Zandalasini, an Italian national. Tiffany Hayes, a former Sixth Player of the Year, signed in free agency, and Janelle Salaun, a French forward, signed on a training camp roster. The Valkyries used their No. 5 pick in 2025 on Juste Jocyte -- a 19-year-old from Lithuania who stayed overseas that year.

Again, their decisions were questioned. Without a star, and without a history of any success, external expectations for the Valkyries were low.

But in the 2025 postseason, this group made history, propelling the Valkyries to become the first expansion franchise in WNBA history to make the playoffs in its first season. The Valkyries were swept by the Minnesota Lynx in the first round, but it laid the foundation for what the team could build on, and made Golden State an attractive landing place for free agents.

For more than a year, the Valkyries knew whom they wanted to prioritize. Gabby Williams was part of Nyanin's original vision of the team, and Nakase met with Williams in 2025 in Turkey to pitch her on coming to Golden State. But the Seattle Storm cored Williams that offseason, guaranteeing Seattle exclusive negotiating rights with the French national. Williams remembers when she heard Lacob make his proclamation in 2023. "I was impressed, and I was enticed. It was like, this is a team I could want to play for one day," Williams said. "I thought I would finish my career in Seattle, but hearing that made me think a little bit. This guy is not playing around; he wants to win. That was eye-opening to me."

When Williams became a free agent, the Valkyries contacted her again, and Lacob joined Nakase and Nyanin in the recruitment.

"He said, 'This is why we are going to win. This is why it would be silly for you to go anywhere else. This is why we're going to have longevity. I want to build dynasties here,'" Williams said.

"Who doesn't want to come to something like that? We play this game to win championships. I've never won one, and at this point in my career, that is the top priority. ... I was so convinced that I would not win anywhere else."

One day after signing Williams, the Valkyries made another trajectory-shifting acquisition, landing Kiah Stokes after she spent four seasons and won three titles with Las Vegas, where she played alongside A'ja Wilson every day and under Nakase for one year. After Iliana Rupert announced that she would miss the 2026 season due to pregnancy, Stokes started every game, defending Angel Reese in the Finals.

Nyanin knew that these players could unlock a new level of her team. What has surprised the GM, though, is how quickly it has come together.

"You just never know if that's going to work out," Nyanin said.

It has. Williams, who was named Finals MVP thanks to a 30-point performance in Game 7, is having the best season of her career. She averaged a career-best 14.4 points and shot 34.2% from 3 -- and also finished second in Defensive Player of the Year voting and received WNBA All-Defensive first-team honors. She became the engine for Golden State's top-ranked defense, while also stepping up to be the shotmaker the Valkyries needed.

"The best part has been coming to work every day and enjoying it. Like, actually, that's a huge part of contending," Williams said. "When the playoffs started, our motivation was just -- we didn't want to stop playing together. We wanted to go as deep as we could because we knew this is the last time we could have a group like this. It's been really healing for me. It's made this season really special."

Down late in a win-or-go-home Game 3 in the first round against the Dallas Wings, Thornton pulled Burton, Williams and Kaila Charles into a huddle beneath their basket. They put their arms around each other and took a collective breath.

"It's just one of those things where [it was] an awareness of what we need," Burton said. "And in that moment, we needed to take an exhale and be together and just be present. ... That's pouring into each other and building each other up."

As Nyanin watched from the tunnel -- and as that sigh fueled their comeback and offered a glimpse of the composure Golden State, a team with no All-WNBA player selections, has possessed since its inception, Nyanin knew that all of the pieces she put together fit perfectly.

"That was the epitome of things we have said to them here and there," Nyanin said. "In that moment, all of the little things we have put together, I took a breath as well just to say yes, they will fight with each other and for each other. That's exactly why I am doing the job I am doing."

NAKASE WOULDN'T LET her players pick up a ball for the first three days of training camp this season.

There was no shooting, no running plays, no offense. The first three days of camp were dedicated to defense.

"That's when I knew this was going to be different," Burton said.

Those early sessions set the tone for what Nakase would demand: consistent defensive intensity, attention to detail and execution on the game plan. It also gave her players a taste of the kind of coach she is -- one who plays battle sounds during practice and calls her players "killers," doesn't allow for celebrations, and believes that cursing just means you're telling the truth.

Even when Nakase's behavior seems jarring -- or as she puts it, extreme -- she has built an environment that encourages her players to speak up and feel respected. It's why they so willingly buy into Nakase's vision and style.

"She's so authentic," Williams said. "We know her intentions are to put us in the best position to win. ... She's passionate. And sometimes we laugh at her, but we also check on her ... it's the love we have for each other."

When Williams arrived in Golden State, she told Nakase that sometimes her delivery was confusing. Others have told Nakase that they needed more time to celebrate the smaller wins. Her coaching staff urged her to take more care of herself so she can be a better leader.

All of this experience has led the Valkyries here, to their first title. Nakase's focus on defense made Golden State's unit the top ranked in the league through the regular season -- holding opponents to a league-low 75.1 points per game -- and second best in the playoffs. Stokes had 31 blocked shots this postseason, tied with Lisa Leslie for the most in WNBA history.

And her players' feedback has pushed Nakase to be a better version of herself -- and helped turn around the Finals when Golden State trailed 2-1. After the first three games of the series, she gave herself an F-minus score on her coaching because her communication was poor. So she turned to her players to see how she -- and in turn they -- could be better.

"You can give the best scheme in the world, but if your players don't want to follow it, it's not going to be successful," Stokes said. "Her willingness to listen to us and our ideas about what we think we're best at and what we can do, that's one thing that has jumped out to me; her willingness to adapt to her players."

Heading into Game 4, Nakase inserted Hayes and Kaila Charles into the starting lineup in place of Thornton and Zandalasini, respectively. Charles finished the game with a plus-14, and Hayes added 13 points -- and the change led to a massive momentum shift in the series, with the Valkyries taking the next two games.

"The best thing about our team is no one cares who starts, no one cares," Nakase said. "We can do that because we have a really selfless team, ego-less team."

"She's a great coach for a reason," Charles. "We trust our coach, so whatever she sees, we'll execute."

As Nakase walked out of her first interview with Lacob, she pledged to herself not to let his WNBA team fail. When she began to work alongside Nyanin, she promised her that they wouldn't let each other fail. As she opened up each season with her players, Nakase made sure they had every piece of support they needed.

All of this has led to history, and the Valkyries winning a title far sooner than anyone -- even Lacob -- could have ever predicted.

"Of course this is unbelievable," Lacob said Saturday night as the Valkyries celebrated. "Two years? It's insane."

stories.headline: Chris Fagan to join the Blues as director of coaching in 2027
stories.summary: Triple premeirship coach Chris Fagan has made the call on his AFL future, joining Carlton as their director of coaching for 2027.
stories.body:
Triple premeirship coach Chris Fagan has made the call on his AFL future, joining Carlton as their director of coaching for 2027.

The 65-year-old stepped down as Brisbane's senior coach after the club's 2026 premiership win -- it's third in a row -- with an aim to return closer to family.

Announced by the Blues on Saturday morning, Fagan will oversee a matchday role and begin mentoring the coaching panel to "establish development pathways for the coaches and help drive an elite, sustainable football program".

Fagan said he was looking forward to making a "real impact" at the Blues.

"While I loved my 10 years as a Senior Coach, this is a role I am passionate about and where I know I can have a real impact in this next phase of my football career," Fagan said in a statement.

"Supporting people to get the absolute best out of themselves is what I love most about football, so the chance to now be able to do that on a full-time basis is incredibly exciting. I can't wait to connect with each person in the football department, and in particular work closely with Josh to help every coach and player be the best Carlton person they can possibly be.

"In all my conversations with [the club] before accepting the role, what resonated strongly was how aligned they were on how to make Carlton a great football club. They shared a clear vision of evolving Carlton into a club that can contend but most importantly, they understand there is still significant work to do to get there.

"To have the senior leadership of a football club share such clarity in their direction, combined with a role that gives me genuine purpose, makes joining Carlton an opportunity too good to pass up."

Meanwhile Carlton's GM of Football Chris Davies said the appointment was an important one to support first-time senior coach Josh Fraser.

"We want to build our football club around good people and they do not come any better than Chris Fagan," Davies said.

"Few in the game have his wealth of experience and ability to connect with and get the best out of those around him. Most importantly, he is a proven winner who knows what it takes to build a consistently high-performing environment.

"Chris and Josh have built a connection in recent weeks over a shared philosophy of putting people first and building a program the right way. With Chris on board, Josh will be well supported, our coaches will be well developed and our program will continue to build the clarity and discipline required to be truly elite.

"We can't wait to welcome Chris and his wife Ursula, their daughters Jessica and Ellen and the entire Fagan family to Carlton."

...more to come.

stories.headline: 'Do everything': Walsh credits Walters chat for return
stories.summary: Reece Walsh says it's "a blessing" to be a sponge around his Australia fullback competitor James Tedesco as he reveals how he got fit for the World Cup.
stories.body:
When Reece Walsh spoke to Australia coach Kevin Walters in August after ankle surgery concerning his World Cup hopes, there were no guarantees.

It is why the Kangaroos fullback's ice pack on his left ankle after the 66-6 win over Cook Islands on Saturday night, in his second man of the match display in the tournament, was a symbol of his commitment and drive beyond the flamboyance he shows on the field.

Walsh, 24, took a knock to the same ankle against the Aitu in Townsville that he suffered a high grade syndesmosis injury to while playing for Brisbane on August 15.

He played through the discomfort to set up five tries, vindicating all the hard yards in rehab that got him selected for his first World Cup.

"I spoke to Kevvie early and I said if you are thinking about picking me, I am going to do everything I can to get back," Walsh said

"He said, 'Walshy, nothing is guaranteed. If you get fit and get your ankle right I will have a look at it'. I didn't go on holidays. To be honest I worked really hard to put myself in a position to get back in this team."

Walsh spent three or four days at the Broncos with rehab and physio gurus such as Lindsay Self and Luke Anning, whom he praised for assisting him in their own holiday breaks.

They told him not to be overly concerned if he suffered a bump on the ankle.

"They generally say that when you have the tightrope (fixation surgery) and rod through it that it is stronger than it normally is," Walsh said.

"I was bound to get a bang on it. I didn't get one in the first game and I got one out there (against Cook Islands) so I feel like it was a good test of strength of it."

Walsh is in a fullback battle with Sydney Roosters captain James Tedesco, who was excellent in the 36-22 win over Fiji last week in the match Walsh did not play.

Walsh would widely be considered to have his nose slightly in front to play in the semi-final against Samoa at Allianz Stadium on Sunday night, but the coach has given him no indication.

"He actually hasn't. One thing we spoke about being in this environment and this team is nothing is guaranteed," Walsh said.

"We are all here to learn off each other and help each other get to the ultimate goal of winning the World Cup.

"Whatever Kevvie wants to do we are all going to support him. No one has dropped their lip or had a sour taste."

Walsh, also a Queensland representative, is a sponge taking in Tedesco's wisdom as he lives out his boyhood Kangaroos dream.

"When you look at this jersey I feel like it is the pinnacle of our game," he said.

"Origin level is so amazing but I also feel like as a kid you play in Queensland or NSW to make Australia.

"I wear that jersey with pride. I go out there to represent not just myself but our nation and my family and the people that set me up to be here.

"I feel like being in camp with Teddy has been such a blessing for me.

"To see someone like himself, the way he prepares, the way he carries himself and the character he is ... I am learning so much."

stories.headline: How Kimi Antonelli overcame George Russell, Ferrari to become F1's youngest champion
stories.summary: How Kimi Antonelli overcame early setbacks, teammate George Russell and a Ferrari fightback to become Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli was crowned the 2026 Formula 1 world champion at the Mexico City Grand Prix, sealing the title with four races of the season remaining.

He stood on the last step of the podium, behind race winner Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton in the Ferrari.

At 20 years old, Antonelli made his title fight look remarkably easy. He laid down the foundations with his maiden victory at the second race of the season in China, and with the exception of the occasional reliability setback with his Mercedes, he remained composed ever since.

It marked Mercedes' return to the top winning its first drivers' and constructors' trophy since Hamilton six years ago, and the team have well and truly unlocked their next superstar -- a superstar simply just enjoying himself.

Here are the highs -- and few low points -- that shaped his title-winning campaign.

- Kimi Antonelli makes F1 history as youngest world champion with maiden title

- Kimi Antonelli's historic F1 title: Every record broken and milestone reached

- In pictures: The moments that defined Kimi Antonelli's F1 title-winning season

Melbourne crash, early favourite Russell wins opener
It was George Russell, not Antonelli, who was the name on everyone's lips coming into the season. Russell was one of the standout performers in 2025, while Antonelli's rookie season had been a rollercoaster. When it was clear Mercedes was the team to beat, Russell was the easy pick for the title.

By the time the season-opener had arrived in Melbourne, it was clear he had finally got what he dreamt of after a tedious four-year wait -- a fast and dominant Mercedes to match his ambition. It was an opportunity he couldn't afford to waste.

To anyone who had paid attention to 2025, it was perhaps not surprising how the opening weekend went. Antonelli showed flashes of pace but a crash in final practice left him on the back foot going into qualifying. TV cameras showed Toto Wolff and his race engineer Peter Bonnington comforting a disconsolate Antonelli after the smash.

Russell claimed pole, although Mercedes' quick repair job allowed Antonelli to get out and lock out the front row of the grid. The race was a showcase of F1's new era. F1's 2026 hybrid engine regulations featured a near 50/50 split between internal combustion and electrical power, but it was instantly met with driver criticism with Max Verstappen labelling them "anti-racing."

At the start of the race, Russell powered down to Turn 1 in a comfortable lead, but a sluggish start for Antonelli followed -- something that would be an early theme of his season. He quickly fought back through the order. A thrilling back and forth contest followed, as Ferrari briefly fought Mercedes for the win, but by the end it was as they were at the beginning -- Russell winning, although he had not been able to shake Antonelli, who finished just under three seconds behind.

Russell seemed overjoyed at the start.

"I love this car, I love this engine!" Russell declared over the radio after the race.

As for Antonelli, the young Italian had managed to avoid the disaster of his practice crash, but he was still tellingly hard on himself afterwards. To team boss Wolff, it was the kind of baptism by fire he expected the Italian would have in his sophomore season now the team was the benchmark car to beat.

"He's literally learning [F1] the hard way, which makes him stronger," Wolff commented on Antonelli after the race. "He was very, very strong on Friday and his pace on Saturday was there. But then the accident happened, and that can happen."

But anyone who thought the opening race of the season was a sign of things to come was gravely mistaken.

Championship standings after Australia:

Russell -- 25

Antonelli -- 18

China breakthrough changes everything
Mercedes showed the first glimpses of vulnerability in China with a series of front wing and technical problems, but it was not enough to stop another lockout of the front row. This time, Antonelli did not repeat any of his Melbourne mistakes, claiming a resounding first career pole position -- becoming the youngest driver in history to do so.

Antonelli had another sluggish getaway though, and after trying to cover Russell into Turn 1, the Mercedes drivers both allowed Hamilton's Ferrari to swoop into an early lead. Mercedes' strong pace quickly showed itself and Antonelli got back ahead a lap later, the beginning of a dominant and assured drive to his first win. It made him F1's second youngest winner of all time, behind Verstappen.

"I'm speechless," an emotional Antonelli said after the race. "I'm about to cry, to be honest. Thank you so much to my team, because they helped me to achieve this dream."

For anyone who had already handed Russell the title after Melbourne, Antonelli's Shanghai drive seemed to be a clear reminder the Brit would not have it all his own way.

It had been a monumental weekend for Antonelli with landmark pole and wins. A week later, he did the same again and took pole at the Japanese Grand Prix, with Russell nearly three-tenths behind. Again, Antonelli struggled at the start, dropping to sixth by the end of the first lap as Oscar Piastri and Charles Leclerc battled for the lead, with Russell fourth. The pendulum of the race seemed to be swinging back to Russell as he carved through the field, but a pit stop on lap 22 from the lead would prove his undoing. Almost immediately afterwards, Oliver Bearman crashed at Spoon, triggering a safety car.

It was manna from heaven for Antonelli, who effectively got a free pit stop, vaulting him up the order and ahead of Russell and Piastri.

"Unbelievable!" said Russell on his radio immediately afterwards.

Russell dropped to fourth by the end, a quite remarkable outcome for such a dominant car. Out in front, Antonelli surged clear, winning over Piastri by a dominant 17 seconds. Antonelli might have been fortuitous getting to the lead, but there was nothing lucky about the margin of victory: Antonelli was looking every bit worthy of his newest accolade and the youngest man to ever lead the world championship. Little did anyone know it then, but it was a lead he would never relinquish.

He would have several weeks to dwell on the new place in the history books, too, with the outbreak of war in Iran cancelling April's races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia.

Championship standings after Japan:

Antonelli -- 72

Russell -- 63

Three wins that broke Russell's challenge
The next three races underlined Antonelli's superiority and marked what would be the turning point in the season. Russell was no longer the established team leader waiting for the next generation to catch up -- Antonelli was in fact fully caught up. After the break caused by the Middle East cancellations -- Bahrain was subsequently moved to Malaysia in September -- Russell looked to fight back in Miami and the sprint appeared to suggest the title battle would swing back and forth. Antonelli out-qualified Russell comfortably but his Achilles heel from the year quickly re-emerged as he fluffed his start and dropped down the order. Norris and Piastri claimed a McLaren one-two while Russell was fourth and Antonelli sixth.

The momentum would swing again hours later. In qualifying again the difference between the pair was clear as Antonelli romped to his third straight pole position, with Russell languishing down in fifth. The young Italian's race start got the better of him once again and he ran wide at Turn 1 while Leclerc took a comfortable lead.

Antonelli and Leclerc fought out in front before Norris came into the mix and headed the field on lap 14. It was Antonelli vs. Norris for the rest of the race, before the Italian fended off the reigning world champion to take his third win in a row.

"This is just the beginning," Antonelli declared afterwards. "The road is still long, but we're working super hard and the team is doing an incredible job."

Canada followed and would deliver a blockbuster moment between the Mercedes duo. It was a Russell stronghold -- three pole positions to his name and a victory the year prior, the perfect place to kick life into his stuttering campaign. Russell started perfectly, taking a comfortable sprint pole, with Norris ahead of Antonelli in third. The mini-race featured a tense battle between the pair, with Antonelli being forced wide while trying a very ambitious move around the outside at Turn 1.

The Italian driver would then lose second after going wide a lap later while trying to pass Russell, losing second to Norris. Antonelli was fuming on the radio, leading to an intervention from Wolff. "Kimi, concentrate on the driving please, and not on the radio moaning," he said. Russell knew this weekend was his time to shine and he ended up stamping his authority and producing another stunning pole, but the race couldn't have gone any worse.

Both Mercedes drivers had a poor start while Norris took the lead before being called into the pits. Antonelli and Russell had fierce wheel-to-wheel battles for the best part of 27 laps, providing some excellent entertainment. Neither driver was willing to give an inch -- it seemed like all of Mercedes' worst nightmares coming back to life, with memories of Hamilton and Nico Rosberg's collisions in 2014 and 2016 while fighting each other for championships.

Fate would intervene before Russell and Antonelli were able to create another, with Russell retiring from the lead with a reliability issue while fending off his younger teammate. "It feels like the gods don't want me to be in this fight," a deflated Russell would say later. Antonelli's win rubbed salt into the wounds.

The Brit needed a clean weekend at the Monaco Grand Prix, but instead the problems continued. He qualified in sixth while Antonelli started on pole at a circuit where overtaking is notoriously difficult.

Monaco felt like a sucker punch to Russell. This time, Antonelli was flawless, taking a great pole. Antonelli's launch off the line was strong, but chaos unfolded behind him. In a race filled with incidents, Safety Cars and a red flag. Russell would be one of the drivers given a drive-through penalty for a minor pit-lane speeding infraction -- one later revealed to have been caused by the FIA incorrectly measuring pit entry. During a red flag, Russell argued his penalty should be deferred to after the race, but he served the drive-through anyway, dropping to the back.

Antonelli's win gave him another unanswered 25 points -- 50 in two races. While Canada had shown the raw side of Antonelli, Monaco had shown his class. Russell's championship hopes were slowly slipping from his grasp.

Championship standings after Monaco:

Antonelli -- 156

Russell -- 88

Ferrari fightback puts Antonelli under pressure
A team in red decided to join the title party and arrived to the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix with its first major upgrade -- and suddenly Mercedes had a title challenger.

Russell responded to his title struggles with pole, while Hamilton split the two Mercedes' to start the race second. A perfectly executed three-stop strategy played into the seven-time world champion's hands to make history and win his first race with the Scuderia, becoming the first driver of the season to end Mercedes' winning streak.

Antonelli suffered an electrical shutdown and was forced to retire from second place with just four laps remaining, while Russell gained some much-needed points in the title race. Hamilton cut the gap in the championship to Antonelli by 41 points -- making him a worthy title contender.

Antonelli lost 18 points in the championship and was downcast afterwards. He said: "I feel very empty emotionally right now, because we're trying to soak in what has just happened."

Russell arrived to Austria ready to fight back and locked out the front-row in what was a controversial pole position which occurred during a yellow flag period. He converted his pole into his second race win by nearly three-tenths from Antonelli, who stood on the final spot of the podium.

There might have been a glimpse of hope for Russell who said afterwards that he was "feeling like himself again." But that euphoric feeling was followed by a kick in the teeth at the next race when Antonelli bounced back at the British Grand Prix. He edged out Hamilton to win the sprint race after making a move on lap 8 of 17 from second. He crossed the line 2.7 seconds clear of Hamilton, with Norris third and Russell fourth.

The Italian took his form into the rest of the weekend with a stunning pole ahead of Leclerc. But during the race, it was the Ferrari man who had a mighty launch off the line to take the lead and win his first race in two years.

For Antonelli it was a race to forget as he scrambled for a point in ninth and desperately pleaded on the Mercedes team radio to stay out on track to seal a singular championship point. He was then demoted to 16th following a time penalty for exceeding track limits when he was struggling with car reliability.

It was a mixed bag of results for Mercedes, while Ferrari continued to build momentum. With the summer races in full swing, the championship fight was far from over.

Championship standings after Silverstone:

Antonelli -- 179

Russell -- 154

Hamilton -- 147

Antonelli strikes back

Russell's fightback did not last long. At Spa-Francorchamps, Antonelli got things back on track, claiming pole with a scintillating lap 0.3 seconds quicker than Norris in second, while Russell had to settle for fourth. The first lap seemed to be another of the micromoments which summed up Russell's year. Already starting down on Antonelli, Russell's electrical boost did not materialize in time for the Eau Rouge/Kemmel Straight on the opening lap.

Starved of power, Russell was swallowed up by other cars into Les Combes, tangling with Hamilton's Ferrari and ending in the gravel. "I'm out," Russell said on radio immediately after finishing. "What the f--- happened down the straight? I had no battery down the straight! Unacceptable! Unf------g acceptable!" If there was ever a radio message which summed up his mood and his season, Russell had delivered it. All of his hard work of the past handful of races, the gentle chipping away at Antonelli, was undone like that. Out in front, Antonelli briefly lost the lead to Verstappen, but soon got himself back in front to romp home to another comprehensive win.

Russell's engine issues would emerge again at the start of the Hungarian Grand Prix, as he struggled to get away and dropped from the third row of the grid to the back of the field. Out in front, McLaren's Norris capitalized on teammate Piastri's late race retirement to win.

Going into the summer break, Hamilton appeared to be just as big a threat to Antonelli's championship as Russell.

Championship standings after Belgium:

Antonelli -- 204

Hamilton -- 159

Russell -- 154

Forza Kimi!

Formula 1's summer break ended with the last Dutch Grand Prix to be held at Zandvoort under its current deal. Russell came into the second half of the season promising an all-or-nothing approach to his teammate's title lead and took sprint pole and then sprint victory to kick the season off in positive form.

The pendulum would swing back Antonelli's way the following day. Antonelli got the jump on Russell at the start before Verstappen crashed uncharacteristically on a wet-dry track. Antonelli briefly got ahead of Norris at the restart, but soon dropped behind the McLaren driver again. A late Virtual Safety Car gave Mercedes a dilemma. Antonelli pitted for fresh tyres to cover the threat of the looming Ferrari drivers, but rejoined behind Russell, who had stayed out on older tyres. Antonelli was quicker but also being caught by the two Ferraris. Mercedes immediately intervened, asking Russell to let Antonelli by into second position. Russell would oblige, despite a muted objection on the radio, and held off Hamilton to complete a double podium for Mercedes. It was odd to see a driver move over for a title rival, but showed how well Mercedes had managed the intra-team dynamic.

Rather than it becoming a controversy, Russell defended the call post-race. He said: "I mean, Kimi was ahead of me anyway. He deserved to finish ahead ... That's always just been our sort of rules, and the fact is Kimi was ahead of me before the VSC [Virtual Safety Car], and he tried something different to, you know, protect us as a team."

The Mercedes call was a stark contrast to the Ferrari team, who at a key moment earlier in the race had dithered on asking Leclerc to move over to let Hamilton past, when the seven-time world champion was on a better strategy. Hamilton later argued it cost them a podium finish, at least. It suggested a team not all pulling in one direction -- and the tensions at F1's red team would explode into full public view one week later at Monza.

Antonelli's home Italian Grand Prix promised a moment of real jeopardy. Issues earlier in the season meant he needed a new engine and the back-of-the-grid penalty that came with it. Russell took a resounding pole position ahead of the two Ferrari drivers and it very much seemed game-on: yet another chance for Russell to try and change the momentum of the season, on Antonelli's home patch no less.

But Ferrari came into the race with bitterness lingering from Zandvoort. During qualifying at Monza, Hamilton -- the driver with the best mathematical shot at beating Antonelli -- had felt he was not given priority when it came to qualifying strategy. "The team was solely focused on trying to get an equal tow for each driver," Hamilton said, referring to the Monza trick of one driver giving his teammate an aerodynamic boost by doing a qualifying lap a certain distance ahead.

Hamilton continued: "We're at a point in the year where 59 points is a huge deficit to recover from, especially when Mercedes continue to be the leaders in speed. So yeah, we do have to work as a team. But have we been?" Hamilton then shrugged and shook his head, adding: "If and when that will ever change, we'll find out."

It seemed to be a clear plea from Hamilton for Ferrari to back him over Leclerc to try and wrestle the initiative back from Antonelli and Mercedes. Hamilton would get his answer in resounding fashion at Turn 1, when he got on the inside of Leclerc's car on the right-left first chicane. Leclerc refused to budge, pushing Hamilton wide and into the gravel. At the end of the second lap, Leclerc lost control of his car and crashed out. It was the most Ferrari of farces and appeared to end any chance the team had of making the rest of 2026 a two-team fight.

Antonelli's car, equipped with the new engine, was a rocketship. He was carving through the field, with each pass leading to a louder roar from the home crowd. He eventually caught Russell -- who had driven flawlessly out in front -- and, after one botched attempt at getting by which almost ended in the gravel -- Antonelli got ahead for a famous and emotional win, the first by an Italian at the Italian Grand Prix since 1966. Antonelli's 26 passes were the most recorded by a single driver at any race in F1 history. New engine or not, Antonelli had turned in the most magnificent of drives, dealt another bitter blow to Russell, and all while Ferrari fumbled a golden opportunity to give Mercedes some anxiety about a two-team fight. In a season of big moments, Monza was the moment.

As he stood on top of the podium, Antonelli soaked it all in. "The weekend itself was absolutely incredible," Antonelli said later. "Definitely so far the best day of my life, and an incredible memory. I couldn't wish for a better day." Two weeks later at Madrid's first-ever Spanish Grand Prix, Antonelli inched even closer to the title, as Norris' hopes of a win were undone by an awfully timed Safety Car. Antonelli would inherit the lead and keep Norris behind with a faultless drive under pressure to win Madring's processional debut event. Russell could only finish fifth.

Championship standings after Madrid:

Antonelli -- 292

Russell -- 211

Hamilton -- 191

Antonelli romps clear

Antonelli's perfect season appeared to hit a momentary roadblock in qualifying for Baku's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, where he dragged his front left tyre into the wall at Turn 1. It was a nightmare moment, a rare unforced error, as teammate Russell settled for second behind surprise polesitter Pierre Gasly. To anyone looking for a championship turnaround, there was historical precedent: Piastri's 2025 season had unraveled with unforced errors in Baku 12 months earlier. Was Antonelli about to trigger the same kind of implosion?

Out in front, Russell quickly got himself into the lead and controlled things from there, holding off old foe Verstappen over a tense final set of laps to record his first win since the Austrian Grand Prix. If Saturday had shown a glimpse of the raw side of the young Antonelli, Sunday showed why he was the champion-in-waiting, as he turned in a sensible and decisive drive to fifth, avoiding further drama on Baku's tight and twisty circuit. Russell's win felt important, but Antonelli had avoided a bigger points swing.

Verstappen's Baku performance had suggested a Red Bull resurgence and he confirmed it at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, a race which was as bizarre in name as it was in drama. A deluge before the start delayed the start, before F1's controversial new engines had a software glitch which caused a red flag before the end of the formation lap. When things finally restarted, Antonelli, Russell and Verstappen all traded places, before Verstappen took control of the race late on. As the finish neared, a final, decisive blow to Russell, as his Mercedes engine packed up a handful of laps from the end. Verstappen claimed Red Bull's first win of the year while Antonelli took an unanswered 18 points.

Russell's DNF was doubly costly, and it knocked him to the back of the grid in Singapore's Marina Bay street circuit. As had been the case a week earlier, Verstappen would control proceedings. Leclerc finished second, with Antonelli having a lonely race to third, but it saw him gain again -- Russell could only manage to fight back to ninth. The result meant Antonelli would go to Austin's United States Grand Prix with a slim mathematical chance of getting it done.

Championship standings after Singapore:

Antonelli -- 340

Russell -- 238

Hamilton -- 229

Antonelli gets it done in North America

If Monza a month earlier had been Antonelli's defining moment, Austin would feel like his unofficial coronation. He could claim the title if he won and Hamilton was fifth or lower and Russell was ninth or lower and arrived in Texas with a spring in his step. On Thursday, he seemed calm and relaxed and by Saturday he was in a perfect stride. Red Bull looked strong but Antonelli was on hand to deny them a pole position, delivering a beautiful lap late in Q3 to edge out Verstappen by 0.179 seconds. Hamilton and Russell settled for fifth and sixth on the grid, respectively, and suddenly the unlikely permutations felt a little less farfetched.

Race day came and it felt like Antonelli could get it done. But first he would have to navigate Verstappen -- the Red Bull opting to start on the grippier soft tyre off the line, while Antonelli and Mercedes opted for the medium, teasing a blockbuster run up COTA's hill to Turn 1. But anyone hoping for fireworks would be disappointed. Antonelli moved across to cover Verstappen at the start -- those sluggish getaways of the first part of the year a distant memory. The Italian immediately started building a lead as Verstappen was swallowed into a fight with the two Ferraris and Norris. Antonelli would only briefly surrender the lead in the pit stop phase of the race, but once back out in front he would disappear again, crossing the line 17 seconds clear of the next quickest car.

At one point, the maths made him champion, albeit briefly. Russell's race was hampered by a five-second time penalty, which turned an already poor event into a desperate one, and he soon dropped to ninth at the same point Hamilton was fifth -- exactly what Antonelli needed. By the finish, both had gained an additional place, meaning Hamilton finished fourth and Russell eighth.

Either way, it was a thumping win and felt like his championship affirmation moment. "Yes! That's how we f------ do it," Antonelli said on the radio after taking the chequered flag. "Let's do it."

Wolff felt like it was the standout drive of his young career. "For me, the best race that he's delivered so far," the Mercedes boss said. "Getting off the start with the inferior [medium] tyre and then controlling it at all times. The race of a champion who isn't the champion yet, but exceptional. So I think he's outperformed the car. Maybe it's a bit harsh to say, but I think his driving style just glues with the car."

It meant he needed just two points from the final five races to be champion and he would need to wait just seven days to start the party -- albeit after what he would describe as one of the most difficult weeks of his life.

Calm, jokey and mischievous in Austin, Antonelli arrived in Mexico City tense and unwell. He would miss Thursday's media session, later saying he felt "very bad." He added: "I had a high fever and stomach problems, so it hasn't been easy. But now I feel OK, just low on energy, just feel pretty tired, so it's going to be important to try and sleep well, because I haven't been sleeping well in these days, and hopefully tomorrow I will have more energy."

He clearly was not at 100% when qualifying came and, in a quirky twist on Austin, when his two competitors qualified down the order, they locked out the front row -- Hamilton claimed a spectacular first pole position for Ferrari, with Russell taking second place alongside his former teammate. Antonelli qualified fifth, which became fourth after a grid penalty for Verstappen. "I'm aware that definitely I haven't been driving well," Antonelli said afterwards. "I felt like already going to qualifying, I didn't feel great, and I felt a bit low on energy, so definitely, you know, it's not an excuse, but for sure, it hasn't been my finest performance."

The young Italian's plan to have a good night's sleep ahead of the biggest day of his life? "Bombard myself with melatonin," he said. Antonelli looked like a different man on Sunday, although he took a cautious approach to the start and standing restart that followed mid-race. There was drama ahead, with an clumsy Leclerc move on Hamilton handing Red Bull and Verstappen the win on a silver platter, but Antonelli didn't need to worry about any of it. A decisive move on Leclerc late on got him into the podium places and he spent the final laps of the race watching the two greatest drivers of his lifetime race for the win.

He admitted the view through his visor -- including that of Hamilton's Ferrari -- was getting blurrier as he neared the chequered flag. "[I was] already [crying] the lap before," Antonelli said later. "I think I lost probably two seconds because I was already crying, basically. I couldn't see clearly ahead. You know, I could see two Ferraris somehow with the tears."

Antonelli came home third, more than enough to clinch the title, to trigger wild celebrations with his team, and his family, who had flown in overnight from Italy to watch his crowning moment. "I am speechless, trying to process what just happened," Antonelli said later.

"A day I will remember forever. So grateful, thank you so much. I am going to enjoy every bit. I'm going to out with my family, friends and the team and we're just going to enjoy all the way because this is a very special moment and one we will remember forever."

The championship makes Antonelli F1's youngest, aged 20 years and 86 days.

Standings after Mexico City:

Antonelli -- 380

Verstappen -- 261

Hamilton -- 259

Russell -- 250

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Real Madrid believe Man Utd's Gabriel will sign for them
stories.summary: Manchester United prospect JJ Gabriel is moving closer to joining Real Madrid  Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Manchester United prospect JJ Gabriel is moving closer to joining Real Madrid while United, local rivals Manchester City and Tottenham Hotspur are all considering a move for United States defender Alex Freeman.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid are increasingly confident that they can sign Manchester United young attacking midfielder JJ Gabriel, according to TEAMtalk. The 16-year-old has been absent for the Red Devils since requesting to leave in September and asking for his registration to be cancelled. Attempts to keep him at Old Trafford have failed so far and a move to Spain has long been seen as the most attractive option, with Real Madrid and Barcelona the leading contenders. There is still competition from Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund.

- Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur are all looking at Villarreal and USMNT right-back Alex Freeman, according to Football Insider. The 22-year-old has caught the eye with a strong 2026, which included him being a regular in Mauricio Pochettino's side at the FIFA World Cup. Spurs are looking for a right-back as there is uncertainty surrounding Pedro Porro's future despite the 27-year-old signing a contract extension in the summer.

- Alejandro Balde has accepted that he will need to leave Barcelona if he wants to get more game time, according to Mundo Deportivo. Manchester United and other English clubs are interested in the left-back, who is attracted to the idea of moving to England. Manchester City and Bayern Munich were interested in the 23-year-old during the summer, although the latter went for Nathaniel Brown. Balde is still yet to start a match for the Blaugrana this season with João Cancelo and Xavi Espart ahead of him in the pecking order.

- Como centre-back Jacobo Ramón is seen by Real Madrid as a possible replacement for Antonio Rüdiger, AS reports. Even so, Los Blancos haven't made a final decision on whether to bring back the 21-year-old or various other players they have a re-sign option on, such as Ramón's Como teammate Nico Paz, Napoli centre-back Rafa Marín and Liverpool winger Víctor Muñoz. All of the players are being monitored by Madrid, but they won't make a decision about any of them until the spring.

- Manchester United, Everton, Leeds United, Newcastle United and Nottingham Forest are all among the Premier League clubs who have been made aware of Monaco and USMNT striker Folarin Balogun's availability, according to TEAMtalk. Juventus have also been approached withe the 25-year-old's representatives assessing the level of interest from various destinations. Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta remains on the Red Devils' radar, but they are also considering Balogun ahead of the January transfer window.

Other rumors
- Borussia Dortmund's Nico Schlotterbeck and Nottingham Forest's Murillo are two of the most prominent centre-backs being considered by Liverpool. (Caught Offside)

- Brighton & Hove Albion goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen has emerged as a potential replacement for Thibaut Courtois at Real Madrid. (Fichajes)

- Tottenham Hotspur are keeping tabs on Nottingham Forest attacking midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White as they plan a potential January move. However, Forest are confident they can keep Gibbs-White in January. (Football Insider)

- Lecce want to keep Tiago Gabriel until the end of the season despite interest from various clubs across Europe. (Nicolo Schira)

- Al-Ittihad are keen on RB Leipzig centre-back Abdoul Koné ahead of the winter window. (Footmercato)

stories.body:
